 JUDGMENT This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

entities.text: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Ganesh vs Hariyan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 10-06-2018 at about 3.30 p.m., the petitioner was a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JD-1129, ridden by one Manikandan and they were proceeding from Sulthanpalya towards J.C. Nagar, on Devegowda road.

When they were near Cupa Hospital, the rider of above motorcycle rode the same in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and lost control over said vehicle, jumped the center median and dashed to the auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-04-C-8313, which was coming from opposite direction and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, auto- rickshaw got capsized, both rider and pillion rider of the motorcycle fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to V. Care Hospital, wherein first aid treatment given and then shifted to Ambedkar Hospital, wherein initial treatment given and then shifted to NIMHANS, wherein he was treated conservatively and then shifted to Basavanagudi Hospital and then to KIMS Hospital, wherein he has taken treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as coolie at Prakash Civil Contractor and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The R.T. Nagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 338 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is legal heir of deceased owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.

Ganesh vs Hariyan on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23206579/
2 4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of one Manikandan in respect of motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JD- 1129 and its validity as on the date of accident.

Further, it has contended that, the respondent No.1 is not the insured of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JD-1129, hence the petitioner is called upon to prove that, the respondent No.1 is the alleged son of the deceased insured.
There is no such relationship and ownership vested with the respondent No.1 to claim any benefit under the insurance policy.

It has contended that, both the rider of the motorcycle alleged Manikandan and the petitioner had drunk and by riding the said motorcycle in drunken condition they have voluntarily exposed themselves for risk, fell down from the motorcycle and sustained injuries.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
It has contended that, the rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries due to the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 10-06-2018 at about 3.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle, bearing registration No. KA- 04-JD-1129?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?

3 . What order or Award?
6.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14.
Further, he has got examined one more witness namely E. Selwyin Jeba Singh as P.W.2 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has got examined two witnesses as R.W.1 and R.W.2 and got marked total 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed its side.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Partly Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
Ganesh vs Hariyan on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23206579/
3 REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 10-06-2018 at about 3.30 p.m., when he was traveling on a motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JD-1129 as a pillion rider, the same being ridden by deceased Manikandan, from Sulthanpalya towards J.C. Nagar, on Devegowda road, near Cupa Hospital, the rider of said motorcycle rode the same in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and lost control over said vehicle, jumped the center median and dashed to the auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-04-C-8313, which was coming from opposite direction.
Due to said impact, they both fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as coolie at Prakash Civil Contractor and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/-
per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 14 documents as Ex.
P.1 to 14

. Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is first information statement, Ex.P.3 is sketch, Ex.P.4 is spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.6 is wound certificate,
Ex.P.7 is charge-sheet, Ex.P.8 is discharge summary, Ex.P.9 are outpatient records (total 2), Ex.P.10 are lab reports (total 6), Ex.P.11 are medical bills (total 31), Ex.P.12 are advance receipts (total 5),
Ex.P.13 are prescriptions (total 20) and Ex.14 is case-sheet.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, on 10-06- 2018 at about 3.30 p.m., when the petitioner was traveling on a motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JD-1129 as a pillion rider, the same being ridden by deceased Manikandan, from Sulthanpalya towards J.C. Nagar, on Devegowda road, near Cupa Hospital, the rider of said motorcycle rode the same in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and lost control over said vehicle, jumped the center median and dashed to the auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-04-C-8313,
which was coming from opposite direction.
Due to the impact, auto- rickshaw got capsized, both rider and pillion rider of the motorcycle fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
Later, on 11-06-2018 at 4:45 A.M., the said motorcycle rider succumbed to injuries while under treatment at Basavanagudi Medical Hospital, Bengaluru.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.7, that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-JD-1129 and the petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JD-1129 in the alleged accident and issuance of insurance policy in favour of one Manikandan in respect of motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JD-1129 and its validity as on the date of accident, is not in dispute.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the above oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the legal heir of the deceased owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest Ganesh vs Hariyan on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23206579/
4 the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above stated facts in its written statement and taken specific contention that, at the time of accident the petitioner and the deceased rider of the motorcycle by name Manikandan had consumed alcohol and on account of riding the said motorcycle in drunken condition they have voluntarily exposed themselves for risk, fell down from the motorcycle and sustained injuries.

But, it is pertinent to note that, except the self serving statement of R.W.1, who is the representative of respondent No.2 insurance company in the present case, there is no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that, at the time of accident the deceased Manikandan, who was rider of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JD-1129, had consumed alcohol and the said accident is not caused due to his rash and negligent driving of deceased rider Manikandan.
Firstly, there is no evidence placed on record to show that, at the time of accident the rider of motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JD-1129 had consumed alcohol.

Secondly, even if for a moment the said contention of the respondent No.2 is taken to be true and held that at the time of accident the rider of motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JD-1129 had consumed alcohol, then also the contention of the petitioner that, the said accident has taken place due to negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle is established, as riding the motorcycle by consuming alcohol itself is a negligent act of the rider.

Further, with respect rashness or rash driving of the offending motorcycle by its rider, the jumping the motorcycle on the center median of the road and dashing the same to an oncoming auto-rickshaw proceeding on the other part of the road, capsizing of said auto-rickshaw, the death of the motorcycle rider, the injuries sustained to the pillion rider and the inmates of the said auto-rickshaw, itself is sufficient to hold that, at the time of accident the rider of offending motorcycle was riding his motorcycle in high speed and in rash and negligent manner.

13. No doubt, all the medical records placed on record by the petitioner and the respondent No.2,
which are marked as Ex.P.8, Ex.P.9, Ex.R.2 and Ex.R.4, clearly speaks that, at the time of accident the petitioner, who was the pillion rider of offending motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JD-1129, has consumed alcohol.

But, for the mere reason that, at the time of accident the petitioner, who was the pillion rider of offending motorcycle, had consumed alcohol, it cannot be held that, the petitioner has sustained injuries due to his self negligence.
Even, it cannot be taken as a ground to fix contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.

The respondent No.2, except relying on the recital in the Ex.P.8, Ex.P.9, Ex.R.2 and Ex.R.4 medical record, regarding consumption of alcohol by the petitioner at the time of accident, there is absolutely no other evidence placed on record to show as to how the said act of pillion rider has contributed to the accident and no effort is made by the respondent No.2 to prove the said aspect.

Therefore, the contention of the respondent No.2 that, the petitioner by proceeding on the motorcycle as a pillion rider by consuming alcohol has voluntarily exposed himself for risk and sustained injuries by an act of self negligence is not sustainable.
There is no law that could attribute contributory negligence on the pillion rider only on the ground that, at the time of accident he had consumed alcohol.

14. The Ex.P.3 sketch and Ex.P4 spot mahazar clearly speaks that, the said accident has occurred beside the center median of 50 feet wide Sulthanpalya to J.C. Nagar road, near Cupa Hospital,
Bengaluru, due to jumping the offending motorcycle by its rider on the center median of the road and dashing the same to an oncoming auto- rickshaw proceeding on the other part of the road.

As per Ex.P.5 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects Ganesh vs Hariyan on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23206579/
5 in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident has not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was negligence on the part of the driver of any other vehicle plying on the said road, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending motorcycle.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1, to show that, there was no negligence on the part of rider of offending motorcycle and the petitioner has sustained injuries due to self fall from the offending motorcycle.

Further, admittedly the Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet filed by the investigation officer has been challenged by the legal heirs of deceased owner-cum- rider of offending motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JD-1129.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary and Ex.P.9 out-patient records, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered multiple lacerations on right side face, tenderness in right molar region, cut lacerated wound in scalp (L)
temporo-parietal region, (L) eyebrow cut lacerated wound and abrasion on left chest.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents No.2 to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false created documents.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 insurance company has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

entities.text:
Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

18. Therefore, for the above stated reasons and in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 10-06-2018 at about 3.30 p.m., on Devegowda road, near CUPA Hospital, J.C. Nagar, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JD-1129.
But, he has failed to prove that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.

Ganesh vs Hariyan on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23206579/
6 19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JD-1129 and he has sustained multiple lacerations on right side face, tenderness in right molar region, cut lacerated wound in scalp (L) temporo-parietal region, (L)
eyebrow cut lacerated wound, abrasion on left chest and for the said injuries he has taken conservative treatment.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e.
pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident, he was working as coolie at Prakash, Civil Contractor and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor examined any doctor to establish that, due to injuries caused in the accident, he has suffered physical disability.

The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered physical disability and he is not in a position to perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his earning capacity.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
ii) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.1,20,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 31 medical bills, as per Ex.P.11.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.58,667/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.58,667/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
multiple lacerations on right side face, tenderness in right molar region, cut lacerated wound in scalp (L) temporo-parietal region, (L) eyebrow cut lacerated wound, abrasion on left chest.
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 9 days from 11-06-2018 to 19-06-2018, in KIMS Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru.

entities.text: KIMS Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.
Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that,
compensation amount of Rs.20,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 9 days from 11-06-2018 to 19-06-2018, in KIMS Hospital and Research Centre,
Bengaluru.

entities.text:
KIMS Hospital and Research Centre,
Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Ganesh vs Hariyan on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23206579/
7
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 9 = Rs.9,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:

As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 9 days from 11-06-2018 to 19-06-2018, in KIMS Hospital and Research Centre,
Bengaluru.

entities.text:
KIMS Hospital and Research Centre,
Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 9 = Rs.7,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Chinnappa Huts, Church Road, J.C.
Nagar, Bengaluru, the accident has taken place on Devegowda road, near CUPA Hospital, J.C.
Nagar, Bengaluru and he has taken treatment at KIMS Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru.

entities.text: KIMS Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.2,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:

The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before the accident he was working as coolie at Prakash, Civil Contractor and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/-
per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do agricultural work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was doing coolie work and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Therefore, notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2018.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.12,500/- per month.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 9 days as inpatient at KIMS Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries caused to him.

entities.text: KIMS Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He might have taken rest for about one month and lost his income for the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.12,500/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 23 years and unfortunately he has suffered multiple lacerations on right side face, tenderness in right molar region, cut lacerated wound in scalp (L)
temporo-parietal region, (L) eyebrow cut lacerated wound, abrasion on left chest.
But, there is no evidence on record to show that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of amenities.
ix) Future medical expenses: The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show that he requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Nil Ganesh vs Hariyan on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23206579/
8 2.
Medical expenses 58,667-00 3. Pain and sufferings 20,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 9,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 7,200-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 2,000-00 7. Loss of income during 12,500-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities Nil 9.
Future medical expenses Nil Total Rs.1,09,367-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,09,367/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Liability:

As per the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner and the respondent No.2, on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the legal-heir of deceased owner-cum-rider and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-04-JD-1129.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that,
due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-JD-1129 the said accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained injuries.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the legal heir of deceased owner of said vehicle is liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,09,367/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,09,367/- (Rupees one lakh nine thousand three hundred and sixty seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 Ganesh vs Hariyan on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23206579/
9 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The total compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

But, due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.

opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries due to the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 10-06-2018 at about 3.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle, bearing registration No. KA- 04-JD-1129?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3 . What order or Award?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above stated facts in its written statement and taken specific contention that, at the time of accident the petitioner and the deceased rider of the motorcycle by name Manikandan had consumed alcohol and on account of riding the said motorcycle in drunken condition they have voluntarily exposed themselves for risk, fell down from the motorcycle and sustained injuries.
Firstly, there is no evidence placed on record to show that, at the time of accident the rider of motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JD-1129 had consumed alcohol.
Secondly, even if for a moment the said contention of the respondent No.2 is taken to be true and held that at the time of accident the rider of motorcycle bearing No. KA-04-JD-1129 had consumed alcohol, then also the contention of the petitioner that, the said accident has taken place due to negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle is established, as riding the motorcycle by consuming alcohol itself is a negligent act of the rider.
Further, with respect rashness or rash driving of the offending motorcycle by its rider, the jumping the motorcycle on the center median of the road and dashing the same to an oncoming auto-rickshaw proceeding on the other part of the road, capsizing of said auto-rickshaw, the death of the motorcycle rider, the injuries sustained to the pillion rider and the inmates of the said auto-rickshaw, itself is sufficient to hold that, at the time of accident the rider of offending motorcycle was riding his motorcycle in high speed and in rash and negligent manner.
But, for the mere reason that, at the time of accident the petitioner, who was the pillion rider of offending motorcycle, had consumed alcohol, it cannot be held that, the petitioner has sustained injuries due to his self negligence.
Even, it cannot be taken as a ground to fix contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Therefore, the contention of the respondent No.2 that, the petitioner by proceeding on the motorcycle as a pillion rider by consuming alcohol has voluntarily exposed himself for risk and sustained injuries by an act of self negligence is not sustainable.
There is no law that could attribute contributory negligence on the pillion rider only on the ground that, at the time of accident he had consumed alcohol.
When the accident has not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was negligence on the part of the driver of any other vehicle plying on the said road, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending motorcycle.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1, to show that, there was no negligence on the part of rider of offending motorcycle and the petitioner has sustained injuries due to self fall from the offending motorcycle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 insurance company has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 23 years and unfortunately he has suffered multiple lacerations on right side face, tenderness in right molar region, cut lacerated wound in scalp (L)
temporo-parietal region, (L) eyebrow cut lacerated wound, abrasion on left chest.
But, there is no evidence on record to show that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of amenities.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Medical expenses 58,667-00 3. Pain and sufferings 20,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 9,000-00 5.
Conveyance expenses 2,000-00 7. Loss of income during 12,500-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities Nil 9.
Future medical expenses Nil Total Rs.1,09,367-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,09,367/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the legal heir of deceased owner of said vehicle is liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
Therefore, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,09,367/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,09,367/- (Rupees one lakh nine thousand three hundred and sixty seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 Ganesh vs Hariyan on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23206579/
9 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The total compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.

Draw award accordingly.
